_comment: Universal right-click contract. Every element declares what it IS (label), how to read its STATE (human-readable text — never raw JSON: that text lands in the menu header and in Prime's question), the question Ask Prime asks, and its own ACTIONS. Engine: prime-context.sh. Prime Linux ships this shape at /usr/share/prime/elements.json.

fallback.label: Bar element
fallback.ask: This is a waybar element on my desktop. I right-clicked it. What does it normally show, and is anything about it worth acting on?

bar.logo.label: Launcher
bar.logo.ask: The logo element in my bar is my app launcher. My session: {state}. What should I know about this setup?

bar.hermes.label: Ask Hermes field
bar.hermes.state: jq -r '(.status // "idle") + " — " + (.prompt // .snippet // .reply // "nothing yet")' "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/1000}/prime-bar.state" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-140 || echo 'idle — click and type'
bar.hermes.ask: This is the Hermes pill in my bar. It currently says: {state}. What is it showing, and can I make it more useful?

bar.whiteboard.label: Whiteboard
bar.whiteboard.ask: The whiteboard button in my bar reports: {state}. What is on my board right now, and does the button do the right things?

items.label: 󰃢  Clear the board
items.cmd: python3 @HOME@@STUDY_DIR@/whiteboard/wb.py clear && notify-send -a Prime '󰆏 Whiteboard' 'Board cleared.'

bar.snip.label: Screen snip
bar.snip.state: echo 'drag a region → action sheet: Ask Hermes · annotate · copy · folder · delete'
bar.snip.ask: This is my screen-capture element: {state}. What is the best way for me to show you something on screen?

bar.media.label: Now playing
bar.media.ask: My media controls read: {state}. What is playing, and is the widget showing the right thing?

bar.tray.label: System tray
bar.tray.state: busctl --user list 2>/dev/null | awk '/StatusNotifierItem/ {print $1}' | sed 's/org.kde.//' | head -8 | paste -sd', ' - | cut -c1-140
bar.tray.ask: These apps are registered in my tray: {state}. Anything here I should clean up?

bar.clock.label: Clock
bar.clock.ask: My clock reads {state}. What should I be getting to right now?

bar.primeVoice.label: Voice (Super+R)
bar.primeVoice.state: pgrep -f 'prime-ptt-recor[d]' >/dev/null && echo 'recording right now' || echo 'idle — hold Super+R to talk, tap to type'
bar.primeVoice.ask: My voice element is {state}. How does my push-to-talk setup work end to end?

bar.audio.label: Volume
bar.audio.ask: My audio state: {state}. Is the output device and level sensible?

bar.network.label: Network
bar.network.state: printf '%s · ' "$(nmcli -t -f STATE,CONNECTIVITY general 2>/dev/null | paste -sd' ' -)"; ip -brief addr show 2>/dev/null | awk '/^[a-z]/ && $1!="lo" && $2=="UP" {printf "%s %s; ", $1, $3}'
bar.network.ask: My network state: {state}. Is the connection healthy, and what is my IP?

bar.bluetooth.label: Bluetooth
bar.bluetooth.state: printf 'powered %s · %s device(s) connected' "$(timeout 3 bluetoothctl show 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '/Powered/{print $2}')" "$(timeout 3 bluetoothctl devices Connected 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
bar.bluetooth.ask: My bluetooth state: {state}. Anything wrong, or anything I should pair?

items.label: 󰂲  Toggle the adapter
items.cmd: bluetoothctl power off 2>/dev/null || bluetoothctl power on

bar.cpu.label: CPU
bar.cpu.state: printf 'load %s · top: ' "$(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg)"; ps -eo pcpu,comm --sort=-pcpu 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | head -3 | awk '{printf "%s %s%%; ", $2, $1}'
bar.cpu.ask: My CPU element shows {state}. What is eating it, and should I care?

bar.memory.label: Memory
bar.memory.state: free -h | awk '/^Mem:/ {printf "%s used of %s · top: ", $3, $2}'; ps -eo pmem,comm --sort=-pmem 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | head -3 | awk '{printf "%s %s%%; ", $2, $1}'
bar.memory.ask: My memory element shows {state}. Is anything leaking or overloaded?

bar.gpu.label: GPU
bar.gpu.ask: My GPU element shows {state}. Is that healthy for an RX 9060 XT, and is anything using it that shouldn't be?

bar.updates.label: System updates
bar.updates.ask: My update counter says: {state}. What should I do about it, and is a CachyOS update risky right now?

items.label: 󰚰  Update now (paru -Syu)
items.cmd: kitty --class floating -e bash -c 'paru -Syu; read -p "Press enter to close"'

bar.wallpaper.label: Wallpaper
bar.wallpaper.state: timeout 3 hyprctl hyprpaper listloaded 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs -r basename || echo unknown
bar.wallpaper.ask: My wallpaper element shows {state}. What should I know about how my wallpapers are set?

bar.notification.label: Notifications
bar.notification.state: timeout 2 swaync-client -s 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tooltip // .alt // .class' 2>/dev/null || echo 'notification centre not running'
bar.notification.ask: My notification element shows {state}. Anything in there I should deal with?

bar.power.label: Power
bar.power.ask: My power element is {state}. Anything about this machine's power state I should know?

bar.workspaces.label: Workspaces
bar.workspaces.state: printf 'on workspace %s of %s · ' "$(hyprctl -j activeworkspace 2>/dev/null | jq -r .name)" "$(hyprctl -j workspaces 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'length')"; hyprctl -j clients 2>/dev/null | jq -r '[.[] | .class] | join(", ")' | cut -c1-120
bar.workspaces.ask: My workspace state: {state}. Is my window arrangement sensible?

bar.taskbar.label: Open windows
bar.taskbar.ask: These windows are open: {state}. Anything I should close or move?

desktop.label: Desktop
desktop.state: printf 'workspace %s · %s · %s windows open' "$(hyprctl -j activeworkspace 2>/dev/null | jq -r .name)" "$(date '+%A %H:%M')" "$(hyprctl -j clients 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'length')"
desktop.ask: I right-clicked my desktop. Current state: {state}. What can I set up here so my desktop works the way I want?

items.label: 󰈔  New text file
items.cmd: f="$HOME/Desktop/untitled-$(date +%H%M%S).txt"; touch "$f" && notify-send -a Prime 'New file' "$(basename "$f") on the Desktop"

items.label: 󰉋  New folder
items.cmd: mkdir -p "$HOME/Desktop/New folder" && notify-send -a Prime 'New folder' 'Created on the Desktop'

items.label: 󰅌  Open the clipboard
items.cmd: bash -c 'cliphist list | rofi -dmenu -i -no-custom -click-to-exit -theme ~/.config/rofi/prime-menu.rasi -p "󰅌 Clipboard" | cliphist decode | wl-copy'

items.label: 󰕧  Display settings
items.cmd: bash -c 'hyprctl monitors | rofi -dmenu -i -no-custom -click-to-exit -theme ~/.config/rofi/prime-menu.rasi -p "󰕧 Monitors" | wl-copy' || true
